The first draft was prepared by Eng. Mostafa Ali Kheder, the document was field-tested by Eng. Sherif Mahrous Omar, endorsed by Eng. Gamal Abdel Wahab, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and Eng. Hassan Ahmed El-Beheiry, and approved by Eng. sections_target.text: Maintenance steps to be carried out

rows: Maintenance can be carried out on the battery with and without load, connected to the charger and without a charger
Connect a 220 V AC supply to the instrument
Connect the red lead to the positive terminal of the battery and the black lead to the negative terminal of the battery
Connect the clamp as shown in the figure to measure the AC current injected by the instrument, which feeds the receiver unit that calculates the internal resistance value — see figure 4-3

Make sure the Receiver unit is connected to both the Clamp and the Potential probe, and make sure the current source leads are connected to the positive and negative terminals of the battery, figure 5-4, so that the total battery voltage does not exceed 275 V
Connect the Power to the instrument
Press the Current On/Off switch
When the Current Ready lamp lights and the injected current value stabilises, start measuring
It is strictly forbidden to disconnect the current source leads during injection

See figure 3-4, then place the Receiver Probe on the positive terminal of cell No. (1) and place the Potential Probe on the negative terminal of cell No. 1, and when the value stabilises on the Receiver screen press the Trigger switch to store the value
Place the Receiver and Potential leads at the start and end of the strap between the two cells to measure its value
Press the Trigger switch to store it
Repeat steps 9 and 10 on all cells to finish the whole battery, without forgetting to store the values

The operator must understand the Flowchart well before starting to use the instrument so that he can know how to use the software on the Receiver and how to store the different tests, print them and correct wrong readings during the test, figure 5-3
After finishing measuring all cells and storing the results in the memory, do not switch off the Power switch on the instrument
Connect the Receiver measuring instrument to its printer using the cable provided for that purpose, 7-pin connector
Make sure there is paper in the printer
Press the Print switch on the measuring instrument
The results can be sent to the computer via the same connector

: Front View of the BITE 2P Transmitter

Digital Meter - ac source current 
indicator with a scale of 0 to 15 A

Power Switch - The power switch is pressed to 
turn the transmitter on and off. 
The power switch is marked with a I (for ON) 
and O (for OFF)

Current On / Off 
Switch - The current on / off is pressed to start or stop the 
flow of the test current to the battery.

3-4 Controls, Connectors, Indicators, and Menus 
 BITE 2 and BITE 2P

Indicator Lamps:
 RECEIVER CHARGER ON/OFF 
 -- illuminate when the receiver is 
 plugged into J4 and the receiver is energized. It also indicates 
 the state of charge of the receiver battery.
 CURRENT READY 
 -- illuminate after the coupling capacitors 
 in the transmitter have been charged to the bus voltage. A delay 
 timer allows current flow to the battery under test.
 OVER VOLTAGE -- indicates that the 
 voltage across the current source leads is greater than 275 V dc 
 (When an over voltage condition occurs, the CURRENT READY light will go 
 out and the current will stop being applied to the battery.)
 J1 receptacle -- The standard 
 power cord supplied with the instrument is inserted into this 120 V (230V) 
 receptacle for ac power.
 Fuse carrier -- The fuse 
 carrier is removed as needed to replace fuses.
 J2 connector -- The 
 transmitter current source leads are connected from the 
 connector to the battery under test.
 J3 connector -- The printer 
 cable from the receiver is connected to print test data. 
 J4 connector -- 
 The receiver battery is charged from the on the BITE 2P 
 transmitter when J4 connector on the transmitter is 
 connected to the J3 on the receiver.
 Voltage 
 Selection -- To change selected voltage: open fuse cover, using 
 small basic blade screwdriver or similar tool. Pull voltage selector card 
 straight out of housing, using indicator pin. Orient indicator pin to 
 point up when desired voltage is readable at bottom. Insert voltage 
 selector card into housing with printed side of card facing forward toward 
 IEC connector and edge containing the desired voltage first. Replace 
 cover, and verify that indicator pin shows the desired voltage.

Figure 2: Voltage 
 Selector Card Orientation

Receiver

The receiver 
 is a universal device that can be used with the entire 
 BITE product family. Figure 3 shows view of the receiver.

Figure 3: Receiver 
 controls, connectors, and indicators
 Power ON Switch -- 
 The POWER ON switch is pressed to power on the receiver. However, 
 it is important to note that this switch does not power off the 
 receiver. You must choose POWER DOWN from Menu 1.
 LCD -- The graphics type 
 LCD displays menu choices and receiver related information. (See 
 the following subsection, "Receiver Keys" for information about keys 
 associated with the screen.)
 Potential probe -- 
 The potential probe is used in conjunction with the receiver to take cell 
 impedance, voltage, and strap resistance measurements.
 Trigger -- The trigger is 
 pulled to perform functions on the receiver, including entering 
 test information.

Controls, Connectors, 
 Indicators, and Menus 
 BITE 2 and BITE 2P

7-pin connector -- 
 The 7 pin connector is used to insert one of the following: RS 232 
 communication cable, bar code wand (optional), potential probe or 
 printer.
 4-pin connector 
 -- The 4 pin connector is used to connect the current sensor (CT)
 3-pin connector 
 -- The 3 pin connector is used to connect the battery charger.
 Buzzers -- The buzzer 
 prompts the user to input data. It also sounds under certain 
 condition.
Receiver Keys

There are 
 three keys located on the receiver that are used to operate the
 receiver and to navigate through the menus and displays on the 
 LCD screen.

The UP ARROW and DOWN ARROW 
 keys are used to select information displayed next to these keys on 
 the screen. These keys are also used to scroll up and down through 
 receiver screens.

The ENTER key is used to 
 access receiver menus, which are shown in figure 3-6 through figure 
 3-7.

Introduction
This document describes the steps for measuring the internal resistance of battery cells using the Avo-BITE 2P instrument to identify damaged cells in the battery.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Mostafa Ali Kheder, the document was field-tested by Eng. Sherif Mahrous Omar, endorsed by Eng. Gamal Abdel Wahab, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and Eng. Hassan Ahmed El-Beheiry, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Gamal El-Din Diab, Head of the Technical Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Safety Precautions
Issue an approved work order
Fence off the work area and place the necessary warning signs.
Wear occupational safety and health PPE
Make sure the exhaust fans are running before entering the battery room
Fence off the work area and place the necessary warning signs.
Make sure the exhaust fans are running before entering the battery room
Tools, instruments and equipment used
AVO-BITE 2P instrument with all its leads and its printer, face mask, insulating gloves
AVO-BITE 2P instrument with all its leads and its printer, face mask, insulating gloves
Maintenance steps to be carried out
Maintenance can be carried out on the battery with and without load, connected to the charger and without a charger | 1.
Instrument setup steps:
Connect a 220 V AC supply to the instrument | 1.
Connect the red lead to the positive terminal of the battery and the black lead to the negative terminal of the battery | 2.
Connect the clamp as shown in the figure to measure the AC current injected by the instrument, which feeds the receiver unit that calculates the internal resistance value — see figure 4-3 | 3.
Make sure the Receiver unit is connected to both the Clamp and the Potential probe, and make sure the current source leads are connected to the positive and negative terminals of the battery, figure 5-4, so that the total battery voltage does not exceed 275 V | 4.
Connect the Power to the instrument | 5.
Press the Current On/Off switch | 6.
When the Current Ready lamp lights and the injected current value stabilises, start measuring | 7.
It is strictly forbidden to disconnect the current source leads during injection | 8.
See figure 3-4, then place the Receiver Probe on the positive terminal of cell No. (1) and place the Potential Probe on the negative terminal of cell No. 1, and when the value stabilises on the Receiver screen press the Trigger switch to store the value | 9.
Place the Receiver and Potential leads at the start and end of the strap between the two cells to measure its value | 10.
Press the Trigger switch to store it | 11.
Repeat steps 9 and 10 on all cells to finish the whole battery, without forgetting to store the values | 12.
The operator must understand the Flowchart well before starting to use the instrument so that he can know how to use the software on the Receiver and how to store the different tests, print them and correct wrong readings during the test, figure 5-3 | 13.
Printing the results
After finishing measuring all cells and storing the results in the memory, do not switch off the Power switch on the instrument | 1.
Connect the Receiver measuring instrument to its printer using the cable provided for that purpose, 7-pin connector | 2.
Make sure there is paper in the printer | 3.
Press the Print switch on the measuring instrument | 4.
The results can be sent to the computer via the same connector | 5.
